episodes.183613: A slow-moving thunderstorm briefly became severe over central Pennington County into north central Custer County, producing hail up to golf ball size along with heavy rainfall. The storm became nearly stationary just west of Hermosa and produced 2 to 5 inches of rainfall in less than 2 hours. Runoff from the heavy rainfall caused several roads to be inundated with water and debris west of Hermosa.
episodes.183678: Mid afternoon through early evening severe thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a cold front and produced some wind damage and hail.
episodes.184360: Although the influence in the local weather due to Hurricane Lee was lessening, the wind flow remained from the south or slightly southeasterly. Under this wind flow, showers moved the Caribbean Sea into southern Puerto Rico, resulting in some water surges and rivers reaching flood stage. Strong thunderstorms also developed along the northern municipalities of Puerto Rico, with gusty winds causing minor damage to zinc roof and tree limbs down.
episodes.184361: As the winds remained from the south, waterspouts were observed along southern Puerto Rico. These systems did not make it into land.
episodes.184439: A shortwave trough paired with increased moisture and daytime heating resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms across eastern Utah. Storms were largely slow moving and some of them produced heavy rain. As a result of the heavy rain, some flash flooding occurred in portions of San Juan County.
episodes.184745: A slow moving cold front accompanied by anomalously moist airmass produced scattered showers and thunderstorms on the afternoon of the 13th. This heavy rain fell over nearly saturated ground resulting in areas of road damage in interior sections of Maine. Localized flash flooding occurred in southern Franklin County Maine.
episodes.184774: A brief resurgence of the active pattern resulted in scattered strong thunderstorms which resulted in reports of a landspout, hail, and flash flooding.
episodes.184780: Complex of showers and thunderstorms moved eastward across central Arizona in the early morning hours south of the Mogollon Rim. Another wave of low pressure moved across Arizona for the second day in a row. Low level moisture transport resulted  organized convection along and south of the Mogollon Rim.
episodes.185666: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed along the lower Trans Pecos during the afternoon resulting in localized severe winds.
episodes.185715: Heavy rainfall produced localized flash flooding which resulted to temporary road closures in the Cameron Peak and East Troublesome burn scars.
episodes.185806: Thunderstorms developed along a frontal boundary over South Central Texas and some of these storms produced severe wind gusts.
episodes.185862: An isolated severe thunderstorm moved across northern Calhoun County during the afternoon. Wind gust to near 60 mph was reported near Port Lavaca.
episodes.185938: Scattered thunderstorms moved east across Graham and Greenlee counties from the predawn hours through the morning. Additional thunderstorms developed across Cochise, Pima and Pinal counties during the afternoon and moved east or northeast into early evening. Large hail dented vehicles in Kearny.
episodes.185992: A lingering boundary combined with an approaching shortwave to provide enough support and instability to support numerous showers and thunderstorms, including a few strong to severe storms. A severe thunderstorm over downtown Atlanta produced extremely high rainfall rates, accumulating 1 to 1.25 inches in 15 minutes. In total, this area received 2.5 to 3.0 inches, but in an hour or less, resulting in significant flash flooding of Atlanta landmarks and residential areas.
episodes.186054: Upper level moisture which sheared off from former Pacific Hurricane Jova fueled isolated thunderstorms in far northwest Arizona. One produced flash flooding.

events.narrative: Flash flooding of Short Creek closed all of the Colorado City roads which cross the creek. The Hildale Street crossing was heavily damaged and will likely be closed for some time.
Heavy rain caused a washout on Clover Mills Road.
Heavy rain caused a washout on Porter Hill Road.
Heavy rain caused a washout on Holley Road near Brown Road.
Quarter sized hail (one inch in diameter), very heavy rain, and local flooding was reported in the Cottonwood area.
Heavy rain caused a washout on Voter Hill Road in Temple.

Runoff from heavy rain caused flash flooding in Ghost Canyon and Box Canyon, and along Battle Creek and Grace Coolidge Creek, west of Hermosa. Ghost Canyon Road and Battle Creek Road were flooded with water and debris. Water and debris filled the ditches along Highway 40 and Highway 36.
One inch diameter hail fell in Kearny, denting a number of vehicles.
The grave gauge on the Verde River at Clarksdale showed a rapid 3 foot rise.

The Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument Big Water Visitor Center reported a flash flood wave along Wahweap Creek that was audible from the town of Big Water until around 8 pm MST. A survey of the creek at the Smokey Mountain Road low-water crossing the following morning revealed the flood wave was approximately 60 to 75 feet wide at some point overnight, which would roughly equate to around 3 to 4 feet of depth at this particular point. This flooding was associated with heavy rain that fell within the far headwaters from approximately 3 pm MST to 5 pm MST.

Runoff from heavy rain caused flash flooding in Ghost Canyon and Box Canyon, west of Hermosa. Ghost Canyon Road and Battle Creek Road were flooded with water and debris. Battle Creek and Grace Coolidge Creek overflowed their banks in several areas. Water and debris filled the ditches along Highway 40 and Highway 36. The Battle Creek at Hermosa river gage crested at 8.86 feet and 846 cfs at 915 PM MST.
Law Enforcement reported that the Big Chino Wash flooded Big Springs Ranch Road.

A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 75 mph that caused damage in the Cedar Grove neighborhood of Cedar Park. Fences and power lines were blown down and roof shingles blown off. The Emergency Manager sent us a photo of a six inch diameter tree limb blown through a wall.
Large tree uprooted at SE corner of Broyles St SE and Sydney St SE.
Tree and several powerlines down Southwest of the community of Bankhead between Martin Luther King Jr Drive Southwest and US278.

The public reported deep, swiftly moving water in areas around the Garnett MARTA station, flooding roadways and carrying multiple vehicles in the flow. Radar estimates indicate that between 2.5 and 3 inches of rain occurred over the area in under an hour, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager relayed more than 40 reports of water rescues, dozens of stalled vehicles, and several flooded buildings and student dorms at Clark Atlanta University. These reports were concentrated around Peoplestown, Vine City and Atlanta University Center Consortium as well as downtown Atlanta south of 10th street. Vehicles parked near Northside Drive and Martin Luther King Jr. Drive were washed into a parking lot near Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Cars could be seen in piles along streets, covered in mud. Radar estimates indicate that between 2.5 and 3 inches of rain occurred over the area in under an hour, resulting in the flash flooding.

The public reported street flooding near and inundation of the Georgia Aquarium and World of Coca-Cola, forcing their temporary closure. Radar estimates indicate that between 2.5 and 3 inches of rain occurred over the area in under an hour, resulting in the flash flooding.
Large oak tree downed in yard of home in area of Bruce Cir SE and Pontiac Pl SE.
Tree down along Henry Thomas Dr SE .
Large tree downed in the 1500 Block of Moreland Ave SE.
Tree down on 900 block of North Second Street in Griffin.
A media broadcaster reported that Rio Grande de Patillas was out of its banks along road PR-184, near Barrio Jagual and at the other side of El Escondite de Don Claudio. The road remained passable.
A media broadcaster reported that PR-3 was flooded in front of Salinas Speedway. The road, however, remained passable.
Several small to medium sized trees and large branches were downed in the Fall Creek subdivision.
Trees were downed at the San Jacinto College Generation Park campus.

A truck was swept away as a result of flash flooding from heavy rain on Johns Canyon Road which runs along a slot canyon in Gooseneck State Park. The San Juan County Sheriff's Office was able to send someone to rescue the stranded driver. No injuries were reported.
Tree down in roadway on 300 Sterling Drive.
Emergency managers from Toa Baja shared pictures of a house that lost it zinc roof due to winds from a nearby thunderstorm.
